correctness.rationale: For every integer n≥3 the local update can be written T(a,c,b)=a when c=b and T=b otherwise. Inductively each full sweep output y has \(y_{n-1}\in\{y_1,x_n\}\), forcing \(y_n=y_1\). On this invariant hyperplane F is exactly a cyclic rotation on n−1 bits. A first-transition count derives each exact predecessor fiber; summing them over the orbit yields the triangular cyclic-run formula, and convexity gives the sharp bound. Independently implemented direct state updates exhaust all inputs for n=3..12 and 3..18, without substituting finite tests for infinite proof.

value.rationale: A nontrivial long-cycle existence example is upgraded to a full global phase-space conjugacy for an infinite graph family. Exact orbit multiplicities and distribution of entire attraction basins expose a structural distinction: the attractors are binary necklaces and their basin sizes depend on cyclic run shape even at equal periods. Sharp extremal basins give a natural invariant sensitive to phase-space geometry, not a routine numerical count.
